title: vibeX docs graph — the emitted artifact
description: What the build WRITES to docs.json, next to the HTML. The dashboard renders it for people; agents read it directly. Every fact in the system appears here exactly once, with its provenance and a computed confidence, addressable by id. Nothing in this file is hand-written.

generator.description: Tool and version that produced this, e.g. "vibex 0.1.0".

revision.description: The commit the derived claims and anchor hashes were computed against. Without this the graph cannot be reproduced.

claims.description: The whole fact set, flat. Read this, not the sections, when you are a program.

source.description: Provenance. `derived` claims are recomputed from a spec on every build and cannot drift; the other two are checked.

spec.description: Spec id the fact was read from.

rule.description: Generator that produced it, e.g. `erd.relationships`. Lets a reader reproduce the fact by hand.

confidence.description: Computed, never authored. `verified` = derived from the spec, or anchored with a matching hash. `stale` = anchored, the code changed, nobody has re-read it. `broken` = anchored and the anchor establishes nothing: the file or symbol is gone, or the repository was not available to check it. `asserted` = a person said so, within the review window. `expired` = a person said so, too long ago to rely on.

detail.description: Why the confidence is not `verified`, in one line, e.g. "bff/src/auth/session.service.ts changed since 2026-04-02".

superseded_by.description: Present on a tombstone. The claim's text is kept so an old citation still resolves to something honest.

verified_commit.description: The commit this anchor was last seen matching at. Survives builds that reused the previous result instead of re-reading the file, so it answers "how current is this claim" rather than "when did the build run".

subjects.description: Every node across the covered specs, with the claims about it gathered in one place. This is the index an agent queries: "what is known about `orders`" is one lookup, not a search.

kind.description: Node kind in its own spec: entity, container, operation, state…

claims.description: Claim ids about this subject, derived and authored together.

related.description: Edges out of this node, already resolved, so an agent can answer "what breaks if I change this" without re-reading the diagram specs.

sections.description: Human reading order. A projection of `claims`, holding ids only — the text lives in one place.

narrative.description: The section's Markdown prose, carried through verbatim from the docs spec.

cites.description: Claim ids the narrative cites, in first-appearance order.

renders.description: A built-in block this section renders in place of claims, currently only "coverage".

coverage.description: What this graph does and does not know. Read it before trusting an absence: a thing missing from `subjects` is only meaningful if the area is not in `unknown`.

specs.description: Specs actually read, with their revision, so a reader can tell how old the derived facts are.

generated.description: Whether the document drew generated facts from this spec. When false it was read only to resolve subjects, so its undocumented nodes are not reported as gaps.

out_of_scope.description: Deliberately absent, carried through from the authored docs spec.

unknown.description: Absent and nobody said why. The build lists what it noticed and could not account for — a subject with no claims, a spec listed in `covers` that was never read. This section existing at all is the point: an empty docs graph that claims full coverage is the failure this feature exists to prevent.
